source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
The full life cycle of a corn plant, from seed germination through to maturity, is divided into 3 broad phases: the Vegetative Growth phase (germination stage, leaf and node formation stage, and stem elongation stage), the Reproductive Formation phase (flowering stage and first grain-set stage), and the Ripening phase (milk stage, dough stage, and maturity stage). Understanding the morphology and life cycle of corn is important so that farmers can apply fertilizer at the correct time according to the crop's needs.

Stage 1 — Planting to sprouting (ការដាំរហូតដល់ការដុះចេញពន្លក): from the time seed is placed in the soil until the root system emerges, or until the seedling has 2 leaves. Water is essential during this stage for germination to occur; this stage lasts about 5-10 days. Germination speed depends on soil moisture and seed health. When soil moisture is 60-75% and soil temperature is 28-30°C, the seed begins absorbing moisture from the soil and energy from sunlight, triggering the internal reaction between the embryo and endosperm that causes the root system to emerge. Leaves then continue emerging over about 7-8 days, nourished by stored food in the seed. Factors that promote germination include water, light, air (wind), and temperature. The main problems seen at this stage include rats, cutworms, armyworms, flea beetles, ants (ទកគូ/ant-like pests), and fungal diseases.

Stage 2 — Leaf and node development (ការលូតលាស់ចំនួនស្លឹកនិងថ្នាំង): from when the root system begins developing and the stem begins growing (around the 2-leaf stage) until the plant reaches about 7 leaves, roughly 25 days after emergence. During this stage the plant is still short, with short, closely-spaced internodes. Problems that can occur include rats, armyworms, corn borers, aphids/beetles, ants, and diseases.

Stage 3 — Stem elongation (ការពោតពន្លូតដើម): the plant undergoes rapid stem elongation, with internode length, plant height, and leaf number all increasing. The 1st and 3rd leaves below start to senesce/dry, while upper leaves prepare for flowering; this stage begins around leaf 10-11, about 30-35 days after emergence. Common problems at this stage include rats, armyworms, corn borers, black cutworms, and stalk rot disease.
